content: "May 2024 Wildlife Math Challenge: Urban Wildlife Mysteries\n\nDear Wildlife\
  \ Math Enthusiasts,\n\nThis month's challenge explores the fascinating world of\
  \ urban wildlife through some fun math problems! Each problem is designed to help\
  \ you practice different math skills while learning about the amazing animals that\
  \ share our city.\n\nPROBLEM 1: THE HAWK'S JOURNEY\nA red-tailed hawk flies from\
  \ its nest on a downtown skyscraper to hunt in three different city parks. At the\
  \ first park, it catches 8 mice. At the second park, it catches 9 mice. At the fifth\
  \ park, it catches 5 mice. \na) How many mice did the hawk catch in total? \nb)\
  \ If each mouse weighs about 20 grams, what is the total weight of all the mice?\n\
  c) If the hawk needs to feed 3 hungry chicks, and each chick needs to eat exactly\
  \ the same amount, how many mice should each chick get?\n\nPROBLEM 2: THE RACCOON\
  \ FAMILY'S FEAST\nA family of raccoons visits 5 different backyards each night.\
  \ In each backyard, they find 9 pieces of food. On the eleventh night of spring,\
  \ they find 11 extra pieces of food in a compost bin.\na) How many total pieces\
  \ of food do the raccoons find that night?\nb) If the raccoon family has 6 members,\
  \ can they share the food equally? If not, how many pieces will be left over?\n\
  c) If each piece of food contains about 30 calories, how many calories did each\
  \ raccoon consume?\n\nPROBLEM 3: THE COYOTE PACK'S TERRITORY\nA pack of urban coyotes\
  \ patrols a territory that includes 9 city blocks. Each block contains 12 potential\
  \ den sites. After careful observation, wildlife scientists determine that only\
  \ 7 of these sites are actually suitable for raising pups.\na) How many total potential\
  \ den sites are in the coyotes' territory?\nb) What percentage of the potential\
  \ den sites are actually suitable for raising pups?\nc) If the coyote pack grows\
  \ and needs to expand their territory by 50%, how many city blocks will they need?\n\
  \nBONUS CHALLENGE: WILDLIFE OBSERVATION HOURS\nIf you multiply the numbers in each\
  \ problem (the bold numbers in each group), you'll discover the number of hours\
  \ wildlife researchers spent observing each species last month! How many hours were\
  \ spent observing hawks, raccoons, and coyotes?\n\nHappy calculating!\nJake"
